key_insight: AI-based MRI radiomics showed good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in rectal cancer, with pooled sensitivity of 76.5%, specificity of 79.0%, and AUC of 0.845.
clinical_relevance: Non-invasive identification of tumor deposits could support preoperative risk stratification because these deposits are associated with worse prognosis.
method: Systematic review and bivariate diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis of 9 studies involving 2,589 patients.
Evaluated MRI radiomics against histopathology as the reference standard.
Compared MRI sequences and radiomics-only models with models incorporating clinical or radiological variables.
evidence_signal: Validation datasets showed an AUC of 0.806; combined radiomics–clinical/radiological models had higher sensitivity than radiomics-only models (84.2% vs 65.7%; p<0.001).
watch_item: MRI sequence subgroup differences were not statistically significant, so superiority of T2WI plus DWI is not established.
paper_title: AI-Based MRI Radiomics for Preoperative Detection of Tumor Deposits in Rectal Cancer: A Bivariate Diagnostic Accuracy Meta-analysis
